body.statement: Always \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}\), where \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the internal outer relaxation that permits the two arms to use different posterior pairs and is not a published marginal-sensitivity procedure.  For the observed law and budgets in \(P^\star\), the worked exact certificate \(\mathcal C^\star\) gives \(L\in[-107500302/10^9,-107500301/10^9]\), \(L_{\mathrm{sep}}=-3461701/31346200\in[-110434471/10^9,-110434470/10^9]\), \(R\in[539509967/10^9,539509968/10^9]\), and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=84380923/150997400\in[558823681/10^9,558823682/10^9]\).  Thus both endpoint inequalities are strict, and they remain strict on a relatively open neighborhood of the displayed interior observed law and finite budgets.  The attaining witness itself has \(r_1=53/100\), \(r_0=6/25\), \(\operatorname{OR}(A,U)=16\), \(\theta_1=247/7<36\), \(\theta_0=36\), \(\tau(P^\star)=-1/10\), and nominal contrast \(r_1-r_0=29/100\).
body.justification: The strict open-set gap demonstrates that common-law compatibility has empirical content beyond a hand-picked numerical coincidence.
body.gap: The internal armwise relaxation removes only common-posterior compatibility inside the present model.  Dorn--Guo's marginal sensitivity model is generally non-nested and informs the sharpness strategy; no published result isolates this shared-binary-posterior loss under simultaneous treatment and outcome odds budgets.
body.consumer: Analysts avoid reporting materially overwide intervals that combine mutually incompatible armwise confounder distributions.
body.proof_tex:
For every stratum and every \(d=(w_0,w_1)\in D_{A,x}\),
\[
q^-_{1,x}(d)-q^+_{0,x}(d)
\geq \min_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{1,x}(e)
      -\max_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{0,x}(f).
\]
Taking the minimum over \(d\) proves the stratum lower inequality.  Similarly,
\[
q^+_{1,x}(d)-q^-_{0,x}(d)
\leq \max_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{1,x}(e)
      -\min_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{0,x}(f),
\]
and taking the maximum proves the upper inequality.  Multiplication by \(\lambda_x>0\), summation, and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) give
\[
L_{\mathrm{sep}}\leq L\leq R\leq R_{\mathrm{sep}},
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}.
\]

We verify the witness rather than treating its definition as proof.  Its marginal confounder prevalence and treatment odds ratio are
\[
\pi=\frac12\frac45+\frac12\frac15=\frac12,
\qquad
\operatorname{OR}\left(\frac45,\frac15\right)
=\frac{(4/5)(4/5)}{(1/5)(1/5)}=16.
\]
The observed risks, outcome odds ratios, causal contrast, and nominal contrast are
\[
\begin{aligned}
r_1&=\frac45\frac{13}{20}+\frac15\frac1{20}=\frac{53}{100},
&\theta_1&=\frac{(13/20)(19/20)}{(1/20)(7/20)}=\frac{247}{7}<36,\\
r_0&=\frac15\frac45+\frac45\frac1{10}=\frac6{25},
&\theta_0&=\frac{(4/5)(9/10)}{(1/10)(1/5)}=36,\\
\tau(P^\star)&=\frac12\left(\frac{13}{20}+\frac1{20}-\frac45-\frac1{10}\right)=-\frac1{10},
&r_1-r_0&=\frac{29}{100}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Bayes' rule gives treatment probabilities \(4/5\) and \(1/5\) in the two \(U\)-levels.  Together with the strictly interior Bernoulli risks and their independent conditional coupling, this proves that \(P^\star\) is a strictly positive member of the maintained class.

It remains to certify, rather than assume, the four numerical extrema.  On the reverse exposure arc, exact rearrangement of
\(w_0(1-w_1)=16w_1(1-w_0)\) gives
\[
w_1=t,
\qquad
w_0=W(t)=\frac{16t}{1+15t},
\qquad
16w_0(1-w_1)-w_1(1-w_0)=255w_1(1-w_0)>0.
\]
For the lower branch, \(\pi-w_1>0\) and \(\pi-w_0<0\), so Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) gives \(H^-=q_1(1/36)-q_0(1/36)\); for the upper branch it gives \(H^+=q_1(36)-q_0(36)\).  Substitution in the two mixture polynomials and the tangential derivative produces the two primitive square-free degree-sixteen factors recorded in \(\mathcal C^\star\).  The signed-remainder variation counts are respectively \(8-7=1\) and \(7-6=1\) on the displayed rational \(t\)-boxes.  Back-substitution in \(F_1=F_0=0\) contracts to the displayed \(z_1,z_0\)-boxes, all of which lie strictly inside \((0,1)\); the positive-denominator test and the original inactive inequality above validate both roots.  Rational interval evaluation then gives
\[
-\frac{107500302}{10^9}\leq L\leq-\frac{107500301}{10^9},
\qquad
\frac{539509967}{10^9}\leq R\leq\frac{539509968}{10^9}.
\]
The exhaustive branch, endpoint, corner, and stationary-cell comparison prescribed and proved correct in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}certificate}\) has strictly inferior rational interval bounds for every other legal candidate, so these isolated roots are the global extrema.  Complementing \(U\) supplies the symmetric attaining pairs and changes \(\vartheta\) to \(1/\vartheta\), without changing the objective values.

For the armwise relaxation, direct substitution of the four rational posterior pairs from \(\mathcal C^\star\) into the active arc identity, the legal mixture equation, and the corresponding \(q\)-formula yields
\[
L_{\mathrm{sep}}=\frac{94711}{277400}-\frac{2553}{5650}
=-\frac{3461701}{31346200},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\frac{212689}{302600}-\frac{1797}{12475}
=\frac{84380923}{150997400}.
\]
The same exhaustive exact comparison proves these are the separate arm extrema.  In particular,
\[
L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}
\in\left[\frac{2934168}{10^9},\frac{2934170}{10^9}\right],
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R
\in\left[\frac{19313713}{10^9},\frac{19313715}{10^9}\right],
\]
so both gaps are strictly positive.

Finally, the square-free factors, one-root Sturm counts, interval-Newton boxes, positive denominators, inactive-constraint slack, and strict objective comparison gaps persist under sufficiently small perturbations of the interior observed summaries and of the finite budgets.  The implicit-function calculation is legal because the certified interval-Newton Jacobians exclude zero.  The two selected algebraic branches and all competing compact cells therefore vary continuously locally, and each positive rational gap remains positive after shrinking the neighborhood.  This proves strict tightening on a relatively open neighborhood, not merely at a single numerical input.
